why: Asserts an in-flight run is never signalled when its schedule is deleted, a defect no other claim names (the existing discarded-sql.Result claims are about telling "no row matched" from success, not about cancelling a running export).
The only claim about an unchecked nil org from auth.OrgFromContext panicking the handler.
The only claim about h.store.Create failures being collapsed into a fixed 500 rather than a 4xx.
Asserts the doc promises five separate unimplemented guarantees; no single existing claim covers that set, and each existing counterpart covers only one of them.
Asserts the doc contradicts itself internally (tiling section vs Failures section), not that the doc disagrees with the code.
The only claim that Validate enforces HourOfDay for a cadence NextRun ignores it for.
About the omitempty JSON tag dropping last_error from the response; distinct from the existing claim that the '' column default is an in-band sentinel.
The only claim about the column list being repeated three times and held together by positional order alone.
The only claim about the missing updated_at column.
Asserts the runtime image may carry no IANA zone database at all; existing timezone claims are about Validate not checking the name and NextRun swallowing the error.
Asserts the objectKey and formatValue tests only exercise already-correct inputs; the existing float64 claim asserts a rendering defect in formatValue itself.
Asserts the whole Validate table never checks which rule fired; the existing test claims are about the untested AccessKey arm and about HourOfDay boundaries.
The only claim that the Format enum's spelling doubles as the customer-visible file extension.
Asserts contentType's separate branch leaves a new format with the wrong MIME type, a different defect from the extension coupling in R22-WK1-01.
Same assertion as the recorded claim that runSchedule stores err.Error() verbatim in LastError and GET /v1/export-schedules hands it back; one sanitization change resolves both.
First of the two identical no-panic-recovery claims, and no existing claim covers it.
The only claim about storage.NewClient being rebuilt on every run instead of cached.
Asserts a trailing-slash-free prefix is forced into a directory segment; the existing prefix claim is about '..' and empty segments surviving.
Asserts the failure branch advances next_run_at with no retry, leaving that window uncovered; no existing claim makes that assertion.
Asserts next_run_at is derived from the run's start rather than its finish; the existing startedAt claims are about the query window, not the next slot.
First of the two identical claims that no code constructs or starts a Worker, and no existing claim covers it.
Asserts runSchedule never re-runs Validate on a stored row; the existing dataset-map claims are about export's missing comma-ok check.
Same assertion as R22-WK2-07 — NewWorker/Worker.Run have no call site in the change — and the alphabetically first id wins.
Same assertion as R22-WK2-02 — no recover in Run/tick/runSchedule unlike the withRecovery-wrapped HTTP surface — and the alphabetically first id wins.
